content: The evaluation of potential candidates for the Guideline Development Group (GDG) involved a thorough review of their curriculum vitae (CV), Declaration of Interests (DOI) forms, and publicly available information retrieved from the internet. This process was conducted by members of the WHO steering committee to identify any actual or perceived conflicts of interest (COI). If conflicts were identified, the committee determined whether a management plan was necessary. The evaluation adhered to the WHO Guidelines for Declaration of Interests for experts and the WHO Handbook for Guideline Development (2nd edition). Both financial and non-financial interests were considered during this process. A significant conflict of interest was defined as including intellectual bias (where an individual has publicly and repeatedly taken a position on an issue under review, potentially affecting their objectivity), involvement in research or publication related to the issue under review, or financial interests exceeding USD $5000. Developers of diagnostic assays were automatically excluded from policy development due to inherent conflicts of interest. Once it was determined that no conflict of interest existed or that any identified conflicts could be appropriately managed, the candidate’s name and a brief biography were published on the WHO website for at least 14 days before the meeting to allow for public notice and comment. During the meeting, DOI statements were summarized by the WHO steering committee. Individuals with intellectual or research involvement were invited as technical resource persons to provide input and answer technical questions but were excluded from the GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation) process and group discussions when recommendations were developed. For the GDG meeting on molecular assays intended as initial tests (December 7–18, 2020), the following declarations of interest were made: 1. Holger Schünemann, Jeremiah Chakaya Muhwa, Denise Arakaki-Sanchez, David Branigan, Celina Anna Maria Garfin, Petra de Haas, Rumina Hasan, Xia Hui, Blessina Kumar, Nagalingeswaran Kumarasamy, Lindiwe Mvusi, Viet Nhung Nguyen, Hojoon Sohn, Sabira Tahseen, and Diana Vakhrusheva declared no conflicts of interest. 2. Daniela Cirillo declared involvement in the evaluation of an XDR test prototype funded by Cepheid and FIND, as well as other projects funded by Biomerieux. She was excluded from deliberations on low-complexity automated NAATs due to a significant conflict of interest. 3. Patricia Hall declared funding from PEPFAR for TB and HIV diagnostics procurement and technical input into PEPFAR guidance. This was deemed a non-significant conflict of interest. 4. Mark Nicol declared research grant funding for studies on novel TB diagnostics, including NAATs, from organizations such as the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, NIH, and FIND. He was excluded from discussions on moderate-complexity automated NAATs due to a significant conflict of interest. 5. Farzana Ismail declared involvement in projects funded by Cepheid, Janssen, and Qiagen, with significant financial support. She was excluded from discussions on moderate-complexity automated NAATs. 6. Leen Rigouts declared research support from FIND and Nipro for TB diagnostic evaluations. She was excluded from discussions on high-complexity hybridization-based NAATs. 7. Ezio Tavora dos Santos Filho declared involvement in community advisory boards and follow-up studies related to TB diagnostics. He was excluded from discussions on Molbio Truenat evaluations due to a perceived significant conflict of interest. 8. Elisabetta Walters declared grant and scholarship funding for doctoral research on GeneXpert MTB/RIF for pediatric TB diagnosis. This was deemed a non-significant conflict of interest. For the External Review Group (ERG) meeting on molecular assays (December 7–18, 2020), the following declarations were made: 1. Lucilaine Ferrazoli, Alaine Umubyeyi Nyaruhirira, Francis Varaine, and Danila Zimenko declared no conflicts of interest. 2. Elisa Tagliani declared involvement in the WHO Expert Review Panel for Diagnostics and funding from an EDCTP grant to FIND. This was deemed a non-significant conflict of interest. For the GDG meeting on targeted next-generation sequencing (May 2–5, 2023), the following declarations were made: 1. Nimalan Arinaminpathy, David Branigan, Daniela Cirillo, Rumina Hasan, Sirinapha Jittimanee, Kobto Koura, Blessina Kumar, Nicole Menezes de Souza, Jeremiah Chakaya Muhwa, Norbert Ndjeka, Mark Nicol, Hojoon Sohn, Sabira Tahseen, Ezio Tavora dos Santos Filho, Nguyen Viet Nhung, Elisabetta Walters, and Yanlin Zhao declared no significant conflicts of interest.
